title: Institutional Nomenclature and Regulatory Oversight
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of regulatory oversight and institutional naming conventions within customs and tax instruments. It captures the transition from legacy bodies like the Board of Investment to modern entities like the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) and the formalization of the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) framework.

evolution.institutional_scope: Shifted from general industrial registration oversight to specialized, committee-based compliance monitoring for trade facilitation.
evolution.regulatory_authority: Consolidation of power under the National Board of Revenue (NBR) for both policy-making and operational oversight of trade operators.

timeline.change: Formal transition of regulatory oversight from 'Board of Investment' to 'Bangladesh Investment Development Authority' and 'Petrobangla' to 'Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation'.
Establishment of the AEO Committee as a specific regulatory body for evaluating and rejecting AEO applications under the 2024 Rules.
Operationalization of the NBR-led evaluation process for AEO applicants, standardizing the communication of information gaps.

Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act serves as the legal authority empowering the government to issue and amend notifications regarding value added tax in the public interest, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
S.R.O. 179-AIN/2014: This existing notification is formally amended by the current order to update specific references regarding the registration and regulatory authority for certain entities.
Bangladesh Investment Development Author: This entity replaces the former Board of Investment in the text of the notification, designating it as the authority responsible for registration requirements mentioned in the specific conditions and forms of the order.
Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation: This entity replaces Petrobangla in the text of the notification, designating it as the relevant regulatory body in the context of the registration conditions and certification forms specified in the order.

member_objects.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) হিসাবে আবেদনের যোগ্যতা

Authorized Economic Operator: This clause sets out the eligibility criteria for businesses seeking Authorized Economic Operator status, including requirements related to legal compliance, financial transparency, organizational structure, and supply chain security.

Applicants must be directly involved in the international customs supply chain, such as importers, exporters, or logistics operators, whereas businesses not directly involved in customs processes, like banks or insurance companies, are ineligible.
The certification is entity-specific and cannot be extended to other branches or sister concerns; the entire organization must demonstrate compliance with all established conditions.
Applicants must have at least four years of continuous business experience in Bangladesh and must clear all outstanding customs and value-added tax liabilities before applying.
Capital and turnover requirements apply to applicants based on their corporate structure, though exemptions or alternative documentation requirements exist for micro, small, and cottage industries.

Logistics operators applying for the status are exempted from standard capital and turnover thresholds but must provide valid licenses and proof of significant annual handling of import, export, or transit shipments.
Applicants must maintain records and business data electronically using software approved by the National Board of Revenue and grant customs authorities access for verification.
The status is contingent upon maintaining high standards of financial transparency and security, with ongoing monitoring and periodic reviews required for all Authorized Economic Operators.

The legal compliance section mandates that applicants must be free from proven customs or VAT-related offences, including tax evasion or major investigations, for a period of three years preceding the application.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue acts as the regulatory body authorized to approve the software systems used by Authorized Economic Operators for data storage and to oversee the certification process.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: Applicants are required to submit a completed Self-Assessment Questionnaire as part of the formal application process to demonstrate their eligibility and adherence to regulatory standards.
Electronic Seal and Lock System: Authorized Economic Operators must incorporate specific procedural manuals for the management, application, and verification of electronic seals and locks to ensure cargo security throughout the supply chain.
Mobile Financial Services: The regulations require that at least seventy percent of an applicant's total financial transactions be conducted through bank accounts or mobile financial services to ensure fiscal transparency.

The evaluation process for Authorized Economic Operator status is governed by the Authorized Economic Operator (Recognition and Management) Rules, 2024 issued by the National Board of Revenue.

The Authorized Economic Operator Center acts as the administrative office responsible for receiving official communications from applicants regarding document submission delays or information gaps during the assessment phase.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the regulatory body responsible for issuing the rules governing the recognition and management of Authorized Economic Operators.
